name: Nauru

findings.local_actor: Cenpac Corporation (state-owned; Naoero Fibre Cable Division / Nauru Fibre Cable Corporation)
findings.financier: Grant funding from Australia (AIFFP, up to AUD 65m), Japan and the United States
findings.summary: NEC built the 2,250 km East Micronesia Cable linking Nauru, Kiribati and FSM towards Guam; it landed at Yaren in August 2025, passed to Cenpac in May 2026 and went live in June 2026.

sources.publisher: Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific

findings.analyst_inference: NEC (Japan) is the cable equipment vendor, so pole third under the equipment rule. Tier 5 from a go-live report (Island Times) after NEC's handover; the go-live date rests on one S3 source. Total project AUD 135m (DCD: about USD 95m) is a programme cost reported in press, not a verified award value, so not coded. Contract signed with Nauru Fibre Cable Corp; NEC 2026 names Cenpac as recipient, read as the same state entity. The cable replaced the HMN Tech-bid tender (NRU-002). Coded after Nauru's January 2024 switch to PRC recognition, with no change found.

findings.local_actor: Government of Nauru (with Kiribati and FSM, World Bank-led tender)
findings.financier: World Bank (lead), Asian Development Bank involved
findings.reversal_of: HMN Technologies' lowest bid in the World Bank-led 2020 East Micronesia Cable tender
findings.summary: The World Bank closed the East Micronesia Cable tender without award after US security warnings about HMN Tech, the lowest bidder by over 20%; Nauru reportedly first raised concerns. All bids were ruled non-compliant.
findings.analyst_inference: An exclusion of a PRC cable vendor, so pole prc, reversal geopolitical. Tier 2 is a judgment: the thing reversed was a bid in a binding procurement that never reached award, so tier 3 overstates it; reviewer may prefer tier 1. All sources trace to the same Reuters reporting; corroboration counted on separate hosts, reviewer may disagree. Reported USD 72.6m tender value not coded as announced. Confidence medium, not high, because of that single origin. Nauru was a Taiwan ally at the time.
